metadata.title: Lyft upgraded, Leidos downgraded: Wall Street's top analyst calls

content.text:
The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.
Top 5 Upgrades:
-
Rothschild & Co Redburn upgraded Lyft (LYFT) to Buy from Neutral with a price target of $22, up from $17. The firm believes autonomous vehicles will drive a "substantial expansion" in the ride-hailing platforms' total addressable markets, and says Lyft shares at current levels provide an attractive entry point.
-
Morgan Stanley upgraded Charles River (CRL) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $220, up from $185. With a strong uptick in biopharma funding beginning to transition into RFPs and bookings, the firm thinks Charles River is well positioned to benefit given its leading preclinical capabilities.
-
Wells Fargo upgraded Carter's (CRI) to Equal Weight from Underweight with a price target of $42, up from $30. The firm cites the company's "improved leadership" under the new CEO, direct-to-consumer growth and "underappreciated" tariff upside for the upgrade.
-
Mizuho upgraded Huntsman (HUN) to Neutral from Underperform with a price target of $14, up from $10, after the company announced a merger of equals with Olin (OLN). Since Huntsman stock should now be linked with Olin stock, the firm is raising its rating to be consistent with the Neutral rating on Olin.
-
BTIG upgraded MFA Financial (MFA) to Buy from Neutral with a $10.50 price target. The firm says the residential credit-focused mortgage real estate investment trusts offer a more discounted valuation than the agency-focused, plus more book value upside potential over time.
Top 5 Downgrades:
-
BofA downgraded Leidos (LDOS) to Neutral from Buy with a price target of $125, down from $200, citing increasing pressure across the "once blooming" healthcare portfolio.
-
Berenberg downgraded Cognizant (CTSH) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $59, down from $81. The firm says the IT services sector has underperformed the market as structural AI concerns have driven an "indiscriminate de-rating."
-
Morgan Stanley downgraded ResMed (RMD) to Equal Weight from Overweight with a price target of $230, down from $286. The company has posted annual earnings growth of 19% and revenue growth of 11% over the past three years, but going forward, Morgan Stanley sees lower revenue growth due to the assumed re-entry of Philips into the U.S. device market in 2027.
-
Morgan Stanley downgraded Iqvia (IQV) to Equal Weight from Overweight with a price target of $200, down from $225. The firm struggles to identify "clear drivers of upside" for Iqvia relative to the Charles River setup, says the firm, which also is "somewhat skeptical" on margin expansion from today's levels.
-
William Blair downgraded Simulations Plus (SLP) to Market Perform from Outperform without a price target after the company entered into an agreement to be acquired by affiliates of Altaris for $18.50 per share or $375M.
